solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Cocktail drunk at social event (8)

blocks.note: high = intoxicated
a ball is a formal dance

annotation.surface: Someone downs a cocktail at a party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' reads as the verb for what happens to the cocktail, but it is the adjective, giving HIGH.
annotation.definitionFit: A highball is a spirit topped up with a mixer in a tall glass.

entries.clue: Head covering up party that’s a surprise (4)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, 'up' reads the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: a do is a party
oh! is a cry of surprise

annotation.surface: A hat conceals the preparations for a surprise party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Covering up' looks like one phrase meaning concealing; the definition stops at 'covering', and 'up' flips DO + OH.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a hood is the soft covering pulled over the head on a coat or cloak.

entries.clue: Reach poor city area lacking hotel (3,2)

indicatorNotes.lacking: the word goes without the letter that follows

blocks.note: a ghetto is a deprived district
H is Hotel in the NATO alphabet; it is removed

annotation.surface: Someone arrives in a run-down part of town with nowhere to stay.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hotel' looks like somewhere to stay, but it is only the letter H, and the enumeration splits what remains into two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to get to a place is to arrive there, to reach it.

entries.clue: Rugby players drinking and behaving cheerily (12)

blocks.note: the backs are the rugby players behind the scrum
lapping = drinking, as a cat does

annotation.surface: A rugby team in the bar after the match, merry and loud.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue sounds like one scene of rugby players drinking; the split falls at 'and'.
annotation.definitionFit: Backslapping is hearty, jovial behaviour, literally slapping friends on the back.

entries.clue: Drops bloomers after removing top (6)

indicatorNotes.after removing top: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which comes off

blocks.note: flowers are things that bloom; its F is dropped

annotation.surface: Someone lets their knickers fall after taking off their shirt: bloomers are old-fashioned baggy knickers.
annotation.walkthrough: Bloomers are baggy knickers, which suits 'drops' and 'removing top'; here they are simply things that bloom.
annotation.definitionFit: To lower something is to drop it.

entries.clue: Wise King of Israel leaving Monday, alone (4)

indicatorNotes.leaving: Monday leaves the name, so its letters go

blocks.note: Solomon, the biblical king famed for wisdom
MON is the calendar abbreviation; it is removed

annotation.surface: King Solomon departs at the start of the week, on his own.
annotation.walkthrough: Solomon, famed for his wisdom, is a stock crossword king, and the comma hides that 'alone' stands apart as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a solo flight or performance is undertaken by one person alone.

entries.clue: Musical about orphan receives one award (7)

indicatorNotes.receives: the musical takes the letter inside itself

blocks.note: Oliver! is the musical about the orphan Oliver Twist
I is the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: A show about an orphan wins a prize.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' is not a container signal here: the musical about an orphan is simply OLIVER.
annotation.definitionFit: The Olivier Awards are the leading British theatre prizes, named after Laurence Olivier.

entries.clue: Being grim, a son needs reforming (8)

indicatorNotes.needs reforming: the letters must be formed again in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A parent says that, because he is so gloomy, their son has to change his ways.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Being' reads as the verb in 'being grim'; it is the noun, a living thing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: any living creature, a being, is an organism.

entries.clue: Taken apart, decommissioned shelters tip over (12)

indicatorNotes.shelters: the outer word holds the other inside it
indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, 'over' turns the letters upside down

blocks.note: disabled = put out of action
a tip is a messy place, as in 'your room is a tip'

annotation.surface: Out-of-service bunkers are turned over after being dismantled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tip' is British slang for a messy place, as in 'this room is a tip'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a machine that has been disassembled has been taken apart piece by piece.

entries.clue: Measure some adopt, I challenge (5)

indicatorNotes.some: only some of the letters that follow are used

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of 'adopt', the word 'I' and the start of 'challenge'

annotation.surface: Someone vows to challenge a measure that others have adopted.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain an optic is the device on an upturned bottle behind a bar that dispenses a fixed measure of spirits.
annotation.definitionFit: An optic dispenses a measured shot of spirits in a British pub.

entries.clue: Serving diners starters of all Indian types in part of mansion (7)

indicatorNotes.starters of: take the first letter of each following word
indicatorNotes.in: those letters go inside the part of the house

blocks.note: a wing is a section of a large house
first letters of All, Indian and Types

annotation.surface: Waiters bring around a selection of Indian starters in a grand house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Starters' belongs so naturally to a meal that it hides its job as first letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Waiters wait on tables, so to be waiting in a restaurant is to be serving the diners.

entries.clue: Chat in which Victor and son exchange locations for environmental work? (12)

blocks.note: a chat is a conversation
surface padding joining the chat to the swap
V is Victor in the NATO alphabet, S = son; they trade places

annotation.surface: A chat turns into green work once Victor and his son trade places.
annotation.walkthrough: Swap the V and the S in CONVERSATION and you get CONSERVATION.
annotation.definitionFit: Conservation is work protecting the natural environment; the question mark flags the offbeat surface.

entries.clue: Happening now and then, AirPods moving about (8)

indicatorNotes.moving: the letters move into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
c = circa, Latin for about

annotation.surface: Someone's wireless earbuds keep wandering off from time to time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like part of 'moving about'; it is its own piece, C.
annotation.definitionFit: Sporadic means occurring at irregular intervals.

entries.clue: Harbour with a large entrance (6)

blocks.note: a port is a harbour
used as is
L = large, the clothing size

annotation.surface: A harbour with a wide mouth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Large entrance' reads as one phrase; only 'entrance' is the definition, and L is its own piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a portal is a doorway or gate, especially an imposing one.

entries.clue: Shining wireless almost put on insect (7)

indicatorNotes.almost: the last letter is left off
indicatorNotes.put on: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

blocks.note: wireless is an old word for radio, less its O
an ant is an insect

annotation.surface: Someone nearly switches on a gleaming radio to an insect.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wireless' is the old British word for a radio set.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something radiant sends out light, as a shining sun does.

entries.clue: Deity really turned against most people from Ireland (6)

indicatorNotes.against: one piece is placed next to the other
indicatorNotes.most: most of the word is used, so its last letter goes

blocks.note: so = really, as in 'so good'
the Irish; most of it drops the H

annotation.surface: A god has truly turned against almost all the Irish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned against' reads as one phrase about hostility; 'turned' belongs to 'really' and 'against' just sets the pieces side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: Osiris is the Egyptian god of the dead.

entries.clue: Crude educational programme for audience (6)

indicatorNotes.for audience: the word is for listeners, so only its sound counts

blocks.note: a programme of study is a course; its sound is what counts

annotation.surface: A vulgar lesson aimed at a crowd.
annotation.walkthrough: The study programme and the word for crude sound identical but are spelt differently.
annotation.definitionFit: Coarse and crude both mean rough or vulgar.

entries.clue: Transfer shocked mentor deeply (12)

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A move to another post deeply upsets someone's mentor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shocked' reads as the mentor's reaction, but it is the instruction to rearrange the two words after it.
annotation.definitionFit: Redeployment is moving staff or resources to a new role.

entries.clue: Raised king, say, in African country (5)

indicatorNotes.Raised: in a down clue, the letters are read upwards

blocks.note: R = rex, Latin for king
e.g. = for example
used as is

annotation.surface: A monarch is elevated to power somewhere in Africa.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link to the definition but is the last piece of the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked country in West Africa.

entries.clue: Desire bit of nice grub to be served up (4)

indicatorNotes.bit of: only a bit of the letters that follow is used
indicatorNotes.to be served up: in a down clue, served up means the letters are read upwards

blocks.note: the last two letters of 'nice' and the first three of 'grub', read backwards

annotation.surface: Someone craves a morsel of good food brought to the table.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bit of nice' suggests a single letter of 'nice'; the hidden letters run across both words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a desire, especially a sudden strong one, is an urge.

entries.clue: Spin drier, an accessory for the kitchen (7)

indicatorNotes.Spin: the letters are spun into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A spin drier described as a handy kitchen gadget.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spin drier' reads as one appliance; 'spin' is the instruction, and 'an' is fodder too.
annotation.definitionFit: A drainer is a rack for drying dishes beside the sink.

entries.clue: Drink is great — putting resistance aside (5)

indicatorNotes.putting: the letter is placed somewhere else
indicatorNotes.aside: to the side, the end of the word

blocks.note: large = great, with its R taken out
R is the symbol for resistance, moved to the end

annotation.surface: Someone declares a drink wonderful, letting their objections go.
annotation.walkthrough: The R of LARGE is moved aside to the end of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: lager is one kind of drink, a pale beer.

entries.clue: Pretty item used by potter holds water essentially (4)

indicatorNotes.holds: the outer word holds the letter inside it
indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence, the middle letter, of the word

blocks.note: a snooker player pots balls with a cue
the middle letter of waTer

annotation.surface: A charming tool at a pottery wheel contains water at its heart.
annotation.walkthrough: The potter is not a ceramicist but a snooker player who pots balls.
annotation.definitionFit: Cute means pretty in an endearing way.

entries.clue: Copper overseas men grade differently (8)

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A foreign police officer ranks his officers in a different way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is British slang for a police officer; 'overseas' makes it a foreign one.
annotation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a French police officer.
